In `testSchema()` the element is found with: ```js const element = container.querySelector(field.selector); ``` so it always expects a CSS selector, not XPath. - For non‑text fields, the schema uses `{ type: 'attribute', attribute: 'href' }` to read an attribute value, not a custom `"type": "url"` field. In `testSchema()`: ```js if (field.type === 'text') { item[field.name] = element.textContent.trim(); } else if (field.type === 'attribute' && field.attribute) { item[field.name] = element.getAttribute(field.attribute); } ``` So with your current schema: ```python { "name": "View", "selector": "//tr/td[4]/a[/@href", "type": "url", }, { "name": "Download", "selector": "td:nth-child(5) > a:nth-child(1)", "type": "url", }, ``` problems are: - `"selector": "//tr/td[4]/a[/@href"` is XPath, and syntactically broken as XPath anyway; `querySelector` will treat this as an invalid CSS selector and fail. - `"type": "url"` is not handled by `testSchema()` at all, so the URL is never read.
